newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico November trade surplus $280 mln -government.
newsitem.headline: Mexico November trade surplus $280 mln -government.

text.p: Mexico's trade surplus in November was $280 million, the Finance Ministry said in a statement on Sunday.
In November, exports were $8.479 billion, the second highest level ever, and 22.7 percent higher than in the same month in 1995, the Ministry said.

Imports in November were $8.199 billion, the Ministry said, an increase of 27.4 percent compared with the same period a year earlier. The government said that seasonal factors led to the increase in imports during the month.
Exports of manufactured goods were $7.170 billion in November, or 19.4 percent higher compared with the same month a year earlier.
Exports from the maquiladora sector rose 21.2 percent in November, while non-maquiladora exports rose 17.8 percent in the month, both compared with the same month a year earlier.
Exports of petroleum products were $1.008 billion in November, a rise of 67.0 percent compared with the same month a year earlier.
Agricultural products exports were $263 million in November, and mineral goods were $38 million, it said.
In November, imports of intermediate goods were $6.499 billion, a rise of 23.8 percent compared with November last year.
Imports of capital goods were $1.019 billion in November, 43.0 percent higher than in the same month last year.
Imports of consumer goods were $681 million, a rise of 43.1 percent compared with the same month a year earlier.
The Ministry said that the accumulated trade surplus from January to November was $6.098 billion.

Exports in the first 11 months were $87.506 billion, an increase of 20.3 percent compared with the same period a year earlier. Imports in the first 11 months were $81.408 billion, 23.0 percent higher than in the same period a year earlier.
Exports of manufactured goods were $73.293 billion in the first 11 months of the year, a rise of 20.4 percent compared with the same period a year earlier.
In the first 11 months, exports of maquiladora goods rose 18.4 percent, while exports from the non-maquiladora sector rose 22.2 percent in the same period.
From January to November, exports of petroleum products were $10.529 billion, a rise of 37.1 percent compared with the same period a year earlier.
In the first 11 months, imports of intermediate goods were $65.765 billion, a rise of 23.1 percent compared with the same period last year, the Ministry said.
In the first 11 months, imports of capital goods were $9.714 billion, an increase of 22.8 percent compared with the same period a year earlier.
In the first 11 months, imports of consumer goods were $5.929 billion, a rise of 22.8 percent compared with the same period a year earlier.
